text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government keeps silent to criticism levelled by Diko party chief Spyros Kyprianou about Justice Minister Alecos Evangelou's remarks about the number of security guards politicians have.
- Two people were killed in separate car accidents over the weekend.
- The vice-chairman of right-wing Disy proposes the creation of a shadow government to keep tabs on President Glafcos Clerides's ministers.
- Kyprianou and justice minister Evangelou are on a collision course over the number of security guards party leaders should have.

- Foreign mediators on the Cyprus problem want to compile a new document of agreement between the two sides covering basic aspects of the problem before the two leaders start Dayton-style negotiations.
- Disy vice-chairman Nicos Anastassiades proposes the enlargement of the party's political committee and a shadow government to dispel any view of an internal split in the party.
- Clerides and National Guard commander Nicolaos Vorvolakos will meet today or tomorrow at the latest to go over details relating to the military dialogue.
